html:
SMTO-GWT-0069 — Programs are still using this GPU, so it wasn't reset

GUID: 91fd931d-c7d1-54f9-86d2-5298519b8c9a
Slug: gpu-active-processes-block-reset
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO found programs still running on this graphics card. Resetting it now would cut off their work, so SMTO stopped first. The GPU was not reset.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to list the processes using this GPU. It shows the names of the programs still on the card, so you know what has to finish.
  2. Let those programs finish, or close them from their own windows or controls. Don't ask SMTO to force them to stop. SMTO never stops GPU programs itself, because forcing them closed could lose their work.
  3. Ask SMTO to check the reset status for this GPU, and ask for the reset only when it says resetting is safe now. The reset status confirms no programs are left on the card before anything is reset.

What success looks like

  • The reset status shows no programs on the GPU, and SMTO reports that the reset finished.

If it still fails

  • If a program won't close, select Copy error details and send them, with the program names, to the person who manages the computer with the GPU. Don't force-quit programs that belong to other people.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GPU reset preflight observed active compute or graphics clients on the target UUID and refused the reset before attempting it.

What this means

  • Reset preflight observed nonempty compute or graphics client metadata for the target UUID and refused reset before attempting it. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Reset preflight observed nonempty compute or graphics client metadata for the target UUID and refused reset before attempting it.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the returned client metadata and identify each workload's owner; do not infer that every listed process is safe to terminate.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the clients in the error details (or run gpu.processes for the UUID) and stop those workloads through their owning applications; SMTO never kills GPU clients. Re-run gpu.reset_status and request reset only when safe_now is true.
  • Review the returned process metadata. End workloads through their owning application or Process Manager before requesting reset again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the returned process metadata. End workloads through their owning application or Process Manager before requesting reset again.

How to verify the fix

  • The workload owners finish or stop their work and fresh reset checks establish no blocking clients.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
